texts.li: [their:friend] {NAME} is in {PLACE}, and the first rider {FACTION} sent out came straight to the colony and asked at the gate for {FRIEND_nameDef} by name. They have not forgotten what {FRIEND_nameDef} once did for them.\n\nThey aren't asking for anything yet. They wanted a friend to hear it first. Their caravans have stopped, and the roads will fill with people getting away from it.

[their:grudge] The rider of {FACTION} read the news off a list: {NAME} is in {PLACE}, and they are asking every neighbor for medicine. The colony was near the bottom of the list.\n\nThe rider left before anyone at the gate could answer.

[theirLowtech,!winter] It started with one family by the river in {PLACE}. Now smoke fires burn outside the walls day and night, the gates are shut to strangers, and {FACTION} have a name for it: {NAME}.\n\nTheir riders are going to every neighbor for herbs and medicine. No traders or pilgrims go in. The only traffic on the roads is people leaving with what they can carry.

[theirHightech,!winter] {PLACE} has closed its roads. {NAME} came in on a trader's truck three weeks ago, and {FACTION}'s doctors have stopped counting the sick by the house and started counting them by the street.\n\nTheir couriers carry one question to every settlement they can reach: how much medicine, and how soon. Before long the frightened will be on the roads, and some of the sick with them.

[winter] {NAME} is moving through the towns of {FACTION} with the cold. In {PLACE}, half the houses have someone sick in them, and the other half have nobody well enough to help.\n\n{FACTION} are asking anyone who will listen for medicine. Their traders are staying home, and the roads belong to people leaving.

[remembered] {NAME} has come to {PLACE}, and {FACTION} sent to the colony before anyone else. They remember the last hard year, and whose help they had in it.\n\nThis one is worse, their rider says. The caravans have stopped, and the first families are already on the roads.

summaries.li: {FACTION}'s caravans stop coming, and people take to the roads, some of them sick. {FACTION} will ask the colony for medicine, and the colony's own people are likelier to fall ill. Help given now will be remembered.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] The rider from {PLACE} won't come past the gatepost, and has a cloth tied over mouth and nose. {FACTION} need medicine, {COUNT} doses, to see their healers through the worst week of {NAME}.\n\nThey can't pay much. The rider will wait for the answer and take whatever is given straight back.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s courier passed a slip through the gate without coming any closer. It is a printed form from their doctors, with the colony's name written in by hand:

{COUNT} doses of medicine. Payment: what we can. Urgent.

The courier is waiting outside to carry back whatever the colony gives.

li.label: Send {COUNT} medicine
li.outcome: The medicine goes out with the rider before dark. In {PLACE}, it will be counted out one dose at a time.

li.label: Sell it to them
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s silver comes a few coins short of fair. The rider counts it out twice, apologizes, and leaves with the medicine before dark.

li.label: Keep it for the colony
li.outcome: For a while the rider waits at the gate in case the answer changes, then turns for home.

texts.li: A family from {PLACE} is at the gate with a handcart piled with bedding. They got out before {NAME} reached their street, and none of them is sick, but the people they met on the road wouldn't let them near a fire.\n\nThey ask to stay. For a while, they say, or for good, if the colony will have them.

[winter] The family at the gate has slept in the open for four nights. They left {PLACE} ahead of {NAME}, and every farm on the way kept its door shut to them, just in case.\n\nThey ask to come in out of the snow, for as long as the colony will have them.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: They are given a corner to sleep in and a bowl each. Before dark, one of them has asked where the woodpile is.

li.label: Feed them and send them on
li.outcome: They sleep one night in the lee of the colony's wall and go on at first light, with a sack of food between them.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The gate stays shut. The family stands there a while, then walks on.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] {PLACE}'s healers have buried more people this month than in the ten years before, and someone there remembered {A_nameDef}. Their rider has brought the signs of the sickness written out, and asks whether {A_nameDef} would set down what to do and send {COUNT} doses of whatever the colony can spare.\n\n{A_nameDef} has read the rider's list twice already.

[theirHightech] A courier of {FACTION} came with a folder of case notes on {NAME} and a request from their doctors, addressed to {A_nameDef}: advice, and {COUNT} doses of medicine to go back with the courier.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been reading the notes at the table since the courier arrived.

li.label: Help them ({COUNT} medicine)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} filled six pages before {A_pronoun} was satisfied. The rider left with the pages tucked in among the medicine.

li.label: the medicine and the notes for {PLACE}

li.deed: lent {A_nameDef}'s skill to the sick of {PLACE}

li.label: Only the advice
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} writes it all down, three close pages of it. The rider had hoped for medicine too, and doesn't hide it.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: Nothing goes back with the rider. {A_nameDef} goes over the notes again that evening anyway.

texts.li: {NAME} has burned itself out. In {PLACE} they are counting who is left, and the count is better than anyone feared in the first week.\n\nThe colony's name was read out at the gate there, with the other neighbors who sent help.

[theirLowtech] The smoke fires outside {PLACE} have been put out, and the gates are open again. {NAME} is over.\n\nThe elders of {FACTION} have cut a notch in the gatepost for every family and every neighbor that sent help. One of the notches is the colony's.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended, and {FACTION} remember the colony's help.

texts.li: {NAME} is over. {PLACE} lost more people than it should have, and {FACTION} count the colony among the neighbors who sent help.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ended; the colony sent what it could.

texts.li: {NAME} has run its course, and {PLACE} has opened its gates again. Fewer people come through them than before.\n\n{FACTION} sent a rider around the neighbors to say it was over. The rider passed the colony's gate without stopping.

li.chronicle: {NAME} ran its course; the colony kept its gate shut.

texts.li: [their:friend] The harvest has failed across {FACTION}'s lands, and their messenger asked how {FRIEND_nameDef} was keeping before saying so. Then the rest came out. The granaries in {PLACE} are empty, and the next harvest is a long way off.\n\nPeople are leaving to look for food. Some of them will come this way.

[fall] Rain came at the wrong time in {FACTION}'s country, then didn't come at all, and {PLACE} goes into winter with its granaries a quarter full.\n\nPeople there are eating their seed grain. Those who can are leaving to look for food elsewhere, and the colony lies on one of the roads out.

[winter] In {PLACE} they are boiling harness leather for soup. {FACTION}'s harvest was poor and the autumn was worse, and the stores ran out before the first snow.\n\nAnyone who can still walk is leaving to find food, and the colony isn't far enough off to be missed.

[spring] {FACTION} ran out of grain in the last weeks of winter, and {PLACE} has been living on nettles and boiled bark since. The first crops are still a month off.\n\nHungry people are on the roads, and some of them will knock at the colony's gate.

Two bad harvests in a row have emptied the granaries in {PLACE}. {FACTION} are eating their seed grain now, which means next year will be hungry too.\n\nWhole families are on the move, and the colony will see some of them.

[remembered] {FACTION} have written from {PLACE}, where the granaries are empty again. "It is worse than the last time. You helped us then. We would not ask twice if we had another choice."\n\nThe letter is signed for all of {FACTION}. Hungry people are already on the roads, and some of them will come this way.

summaries.li: Hungry travelers and pilgrims come more often. {FACTION} will ask the colony for food, and some of the desperate may try their luck against its walls. Food given now will be remembered.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] A cart from {PLACE} has come to the gate behind two thin oxen, with nothing in the back. {FACTION} ask for {COUNT} portions of food, any kind, for the old and the very young.\n\nThey can pay something, the driver says, in silver they had been keeping back for seed.

[theirHightech] A truck from {PLACE} has coasted up to the gate on the last of its fuel, its bed swept clean. {FACTION} ask for {COUNT} portions of food, any kind, for the old and the very young.\n\nThey can pay. A grain dealer in the next valley is asking four times the usual price, the driver says, and getting it.

li.label: Send {COUNT} food
li.outcome: The driver loads the food at the gate and shakes hands with everyone who carried a sack. It will be in {PLACE} by tomorrow.

li.label: Sell it at a fair price
li.outcome: The driver counts out the usual price and loads the food. Most of the region is charging {FACTION} more this year.
li.deed: sold food to {PLACE} at a fair price

li.label: Sell it dear
li.outcome: {FACTION} pay four times what the food is worth. The driver counts it out without a word and loads the sacks alone.
li.deed: sold food to {PLACE} at famine prices

li.label: Nothing to spare
li.outcome: The driver turns around at the gate and goes back the way they came, empty.

texts.li: A family from the villages around {PLACE} has walked for days to get here. They ask for work. Any work, the eldest says, for food and a roof, and holds out a pair of hands as hard as boot leather.
[winter] People from {PLACE} are at the gate, thin and blue with cold, asking for work in exchange for food. They walked here through the snow because they heard the colony still eats every day.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: They are fed first, then shown where to sleep. The next morning they are up before anyone else, asking what needs doing.

li.label: Feed them and send them on
li.outcome: They eat at the gate, sleep under the eaves and go on at first light with a bundle of food.

li.label: food for the hungry on the road
Turn them away
li.outcome: They are told there's no work and no food to spare. They go.

li.label: The hungry come
li.text: Hunger has driven the raiders of {ENEMY} out early this year, and the colony's stores are the only full ones for days around.

texts.li: The first new grain is in at {PLACE}, and the worst is over for {FACTION}.\n\nSome of what they ate came up the road from the colony, and in {PLACE} they have started calling it the bread road.

[winter] Spring is still weeks away, but a relief caravan reached {PLACE} at last, and the people there have stopped boiling leather.\n\nUntil it came, {FACTION} lived partly on the colony's food, and they have not been quiet about it.

li.chronicle: The famine among {FACTION} ended; they remember the colony's food.

texts.li: The famine is over, and {FACTION} have started counting what it cost them. The colony's prices are on that list, near the top.\n\nIn {PLACE} the colony is the place that sold bread at four times its worth, and that is how they will tell it.

li.chronicle: The famine among {FACTION} ended; they remember what the colony charged.

texts.li: {FACTION} have come through the famine, thinner and quieter, and some of what kept {PLACE} going came from the colony.

li.chronicle: The famine among {FACTION} ended; some of their bread had come from the colony.

texts.li: The famine among {FACTION} is over. {PLACE} came out of it smaller, and buried more of its old people than it should have.\n\n{FACTION} know the colony's granary was full the whole time.

li.chronicle: The famine among {FACTION} ended; the colony kept its stores to itself.

texts.li: [their:grateful] The snow has closed the passes, and {FACTION} are burning their chairs in {PLACE} to keep warm. The first sledge they sent out came this way, to the friends they remember.\n\nThe whole region is in for a long winter.

[theirLowtech] The old people in {PLACE} say they have never seen snow like it. The passes are closed, the river is frozen to the bottom at the shallows, and {FACTION} have brought their goats into the houses.\n\nIt will be a long winter for everyone in the region, and longer for anyone without a full woodpile.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s fuel lines froze two weeks ago, and {PLACE} has rationed heat by the hour ever since. The roads are shut under drifts as high as a truck.\n\nAnyone in the region without fuel put by is in for a bad few weeks.

[fall] Winter has come early, and hard. The first snow fell on the harvest in {PLACE} before half of it was in, and it hasn't stopped since.\n\n{FACTION} are digging cabbages out of the drifts. So is every farm in the region.

summaries.li: Cold snaps come more often, and traders and visitors stay home. {FACTION} will need firewood, and travelers caught by the snow may knock at the gate.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] A sledge from {PLACE} came up the frozen river this morning. {FACTION} are out of firewood and out of dry trees to cut, and ask for {COUNT} logs to see the old and the sick through the worst of it.\n\nThey'll pay what they can. It isn't much.

[theirHightech] {FACTION} have run their generators dry, and {PLACE} is heating with wood again, the way their grandparents did. Their sledge is at the gate with chains for {COUNT} logs, and the driver says they will pay what they can.

li.label: Send {COUNT} wood
li.outcome: The sledge goes back to {PLACE} stacked so high that the driver walks beside it.

li.label: Sell it to them
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s driver pays a fair price, chains the logs down and starts back while there's still light.

li.label: Keep it
li.outcome: The sledge turns around empty. The colony's woodpile stays where it is, against a winter that may run long here too.

texts.li: Two travelers of {FACTION} came in out of the snow at dusk, caught between towns when the road closed. They ask to stay until it opens again, however long that takes.\n\nThey will eat for two and work for half that, one of them admits. They will also remember it.

li.label: Shelter them until the thaw
li.outcome: The travelers get a dry corner and a place near the fire, and promise to make it good when the roads open.

li.label: Point them to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The travelers are given the way to {PLACE} and a stick each to test the drifts with, and set off into the snow.

texts.li: [helped,theirLowtech] The ice on the river broke last night with a sound like a felled tree. The worst of the winter is over.\n\n{FACTION} came through it, and they know the colony's part in that.

[helped,theirHightech] The plows have reached {PLACE}, {FACTION} have their power back, and the cold is breaking.\n\nThe colony's help is part of how they got through it, and they have said so in every town their first convoys reached.
[ignored] The cold has broken. {PLACE} is digging out, and the roads are opening one by one.\n\n{PLACE} lost people to the cold this year, and got through the rest of it without the colony.

{FACTION} lost every field around {PLACE} in a single afternoon. The cloud that did it is still out there: a swarm of locusts as wide as a valley, and it hasn't settled yet.\n\nWhether it comes this way is up to the wind.

[summer] The sky to the south went brown at midday, and a few minutes later came the sound, like rain that doesn't stop. Locusts. By evening a rider had brought word that {PLACE} was stripped to the dirt.\n\nThe swarm is still in the air.

summaries.li: Any day now the swarm may pass over the colony and strip its open fields. Roofed fields and greenhouses are safe, and smoke may turn it. Food will be scarcer in the region for a while.
[struck] The swarm has been and gone. Food will be scarcer in the region for a while.

texts.li: "Smoke," {A_nameDef} says. "Smudge fires the length of the fields, fed day and night. They lift and go around." Others want every ripe plant cut and under a roof before the swarm can get to it. A few want both.\n\n{A_nameDef} has already started stacking wood by the fields.

li.label: Light smudge fires ({COUNT} wood)
li.outcome: The smudge fires burn along the field edges day and night, and the smoke gets into everyone's bedding.

li.label: the watch over the smudge fires
Harvest what's ripe
li.outcome: Everything ripe in the open fields is cut and brought in. What's still green stays in the ground and takes its chances.

li.label: Both
li.outcome: The smudge fires are lit and the ripe crops come in. For a week the colony works tired and smells of smoke.

li.label: Leave it to luck
li.outcome: The colony goes on as usual and keeps an eye on the sky.

texts.li: The swarm has gone east. The smoke turned most of it from the colony's fields, and what it did take in the open will grow back.\n\n{FACTION} had no smoke to spare. They lost nearly everything around {PLACE}.

li.chronicle: The locusts passed; the colony's smoke saved most of its fields.

texts.li: [!harvested] The swarm has moved on, leaving the colony's open fields bare and the whole region poorer. What was under a roof came through.
[harvested] The open fields are stubble now, and the swarm has moved on. The ripe crops were in before it came, and the plants under a roof were never touched.

li.chronicle: The locusts passed, and stripped the colony's open fields.

texts.li: [smoke] Whether it was the smoke or the wind, the swarm went around the colony and on to the east. The fields are untouched.\n\n{FACTION} were not so lucky. {PLACE} will be hungry this year.
[!smoke] The swarm passed a valley to the north and kept going. The colony's fields are untouched, for no reason anyone can find.\n\nAt {PLACE} they are replanting what they can, late in the season.

li.chronicle: The locusts passed the colony by.

texts.li: The swarm comes down

[!smoke] The swarm came over the hill at noon and settled on the colony's fields like a brown snow. By evening it had lifted and gone, and so had the crops: {COUNT} plants in the open fields were stripped or flattened.\n\nWhat was under a roof came through untouched.

[smoke] The smoke turned most of the swarm, but not all of it. A tail of it came down on the colony's fields at noon and was gone by evening, leaving {COUNT} plants in the open stripped or flattened.\n\nThe rest of the fields stood in the smoke and were left alone.

[their:friend] The river burst its banks in the night and took the lower half of {PLACE}. {FACTION} are camped on the hills above the town, and they've sent a boy up the river path to ask whether {FRIEND_nameDef} and the colony can help.\n\nThe colony's own stretch of the river is high and brown, but holding.

The river has been rising for a week, and last night it broke its banks downstream. {PLACE} sits on the low ground by the water, and most of it is under water now.\n\n{FACTION} are moving to higher ground with whatever they could save. Up here, the river is a hand's width from the top of the bank and full of branches.

[spring] The snowmelt came in a single week this year. The river burst its banks below the colony in the night and took the lower half of {PLACE} with it: houses, mills, the bridge.\n\n{FACTION} are camped on the hills above the town, waiting for the water to go down.

summaries.li: People from {PLACE} may come asking for shelter, {FACTION} will need timber to rebuild, and the river will carry down some of what the flood took.

texts.li: Wet to the waist, a family from {PLACE} came up the river path this morning with a goat and a sack of seed. Their house is gone.\n\nThey ask whether the colony has room. They are not proud about it.

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: The family gets dry clothes, a hot meal and a place to sleep. The goat gets the pen.
li.deed: took in a family flooded out of {PLACE}

li.label: Feed them and send them on
li.outcome: They are fed and dried out, and they go on toward the hills where the rest of {FACTION} are camped.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The family is told the colony has no room. They go back down the river path, the goat pulling at its rope.

texts.li: The water has gone down at {PLACE}, and {FACTION} are rebuilding. Everything they had stored is mud, and their foreman has come up the river road to ask the colony for {COUNT} logs: roofs first, then the mill.\n\nTheir carts can come up for the timber. They can pay something for it, if not much.

li.label: Send {COUNT} wood
li.outcome: Carts come up the river road for the timber and go back down it loaded. There will be colony wood in the new roofs of {PLACE}.

li.label: Sell it to them
li.outcome: {FACTION}'s carters pay for the timber at the gate and take it back down the river road.

li.label: Keep it
li.outcome: The colony keeps its timber. {FACTION} will find it somewhere else.

texts.li: The water has dropped enough to walk the bank, and the flood has left things in the reeds: crates, a cart wheel, a door with the paint still on it. {A_nameDef} pulled out what was worth keeping and brought it up to the colony.\n\nSome of it was somebody's in {PLACE}. There's no telling whose.
[helped] The river is back in its bed, and {PLACE} is half rebuilt. {FACTION} have put a mark on the new mill where the water reached, and next to it, they say, the colony's name.
[ignored] {FACTION} are rebuilding {PLACE} on higher ground, now that the river is back in its bed. It will take years.
